# Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

Reviewed by /plan-ceo-review on 2026-09-10 (mode: HOLD SCOPE). Original plan content is
preserved below; accepted amendments are marked `[Amended: D<n>]` and cross-reference the
decision and finding registries in the review record.

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key
  single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters.

`[Amended: D3, D4, D5, D7]` The original sketch stated that no coordination between a
cache fill and a write was needed. Review finding F1 shows that claim violates the
retained read-after-write contract (see Async schedule in the review record). The
complete read/write ordering rules are now:

1. A miss registers an in-flight fill for the key in the existing single-flight
   wrapper. The fill handle carries an `invalidated` flag.
2. A write marks and detaches the key's in-flight fill before awaiting the DB, and
   again after the write settles (success, typed failure, or indeterminate failure),
   then deletes the key. A detached fill still resolves for its own waiters (allowed by
   the contract) but never populates the cache; it increments `profile_cache.fill_discarded`.
3. Absent results are stored as the sentinel with the 10-second TTL and mapped back to
   the repository's existing absent result on a hit, so callers see identical behavior
   with and without the cache. Values use the 30-second TTL.
4. The feature flag is evaluated once per operation with the same deterministic key
   hash for reads and writes. A flag-read failure evaluates as disabled. Any change to
   the flag value (off/on or percentage) reinitializes an empty cache and invalidates
   all in-flight fills.

```javascript
// Fill/write ordering (F1, F3): a fill that overlaps any write never populates.
//   miss ─▶ flight{invalidated:false} ─▶ await repository.read ─▶ invalidated ? discard : set
//   write ─▶ invalidate(key) ─▶ await repository.write ─▶ finally: invalidate(key); cache.delete(key)
async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!flag.enabledFor(key)) return repository.read(key);        // flag error => disabled (F5)
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return fromCacheValue(cached);        // sentinel -> existing absent result (F2)
  return singleFlight.run(key, async (flight) => {
    const value = await repository.read(key);                     // typed errors propagate; nothing cached
    if (flight.invalidated) metrics.increment('profile_cache.fill_discarded');
    else cache.set(key, toCacheValue(value), ttlFor(value));      // 30 s value / 10 s sentinel (F2)
    return value;
  });
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  if (!flag.enabledFor(key)) return repository.write(key, update);
  singleFlight.invalidate(key);      // fills started before the write cannot populate (F1)
  try {
    return await repository.write(key, update);
  } finally {
    singleFlight.invalidate(key);    // fills issued during the write are pre-commit snapshots (F1)
    cache.delete(key);               // every outcome, including indeterminate failures (F3)
  }
}
```

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. New wrapper tests cover hit/miss,
eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure fallback, successful-write
invalidation, and concurrent-miss coalescing.

`[Amended: D3, D4, D5, D7]` Additional required tests (see Section 6 and tasks T1 to T4):
controlled-schedule read-after-write tests for both completion orders and for a fill
issued during a write; sentinel round-trip and negative-cache tests; write-failure
invalidation (replaces the original "failed-write preservation" test, which asserted the
prohibited stale result after an ambiguous-outcome commit); flag-change flush and
in-flight discard; same-hash flag evaluation for reads and writes; TTL tests use fake timers.

The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,
then 50%, then all keys after one healthy hour at each stage. Monitor hit/miss,
eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95 without raw IDs.
On error-rate or latency regression, disable the flag immediately; both reads
and writes bypass the cache while disabled, and enabling creates an empty cache.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors
the rollout and records the results against the acceptance targets.

`[Amended: D6]` "Healthy hour" is defined and alerted (task T5): error rate within the
existing SLO, read p95 not above baseline, zero adapter fallback errors, cache in ACTIVE
state, `fill_discarded` below 1% of fills, and at the 100% stage hit ratio at least 60%
after a 5-minute warmup. A day-1 dashboard, alerts, and a runbook are deliverables of
this change, not follow-ups.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.

Post-deploy: first 5 minutes check fallback errors zero and hit ratio climbing; first hour check p95, DB CPU, error rate against the health definition.
10. **Long-term trajectory.** Reversibility 5/5 (flag off, then delete the wrapper). Debt: none beyond a code-comment diagram of fill/write ordering, included in T1. # Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

Reviewed by /plan-ceo-review on 2026-09-10 (HOLD SCOPE, spawned run: every decision
auto-selected the recommended option; see Decision Register). Original plan content is
preserved below; amendments are marked `[Amended: F#]` and point at the finding record.

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

`[Amended: F7]` Targets are unchanged. Hit rate is measured over flag-enabled keys
only, and read latency is recorded separately for hits and misses so the owner can
attribute any p95 result (see Metric Schema).

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. Absent records use a
  distinct sentinel with a 10-second TTL; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key
  single-flight wrapper coalesces simultaneous misses and releases on failure.
- A read already in progress when a write commits may return its earlier DB
  snapshot to that caller. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.

`[Amended: F1]` Boundary definition used by this plan: a write "completes" when
`writeProfile` resolves to its caller. `invalidate()` runs synchronously inside that
same continuation, before resolution, so any read that begins after the caller
observes completion cannot hit a pre-write entry or join a pre-write DB read.

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters.

`[Amended: F1, F2, F4, F10]` The original sketch stated that no coordination between a
cache fill and a write was proposed. The review showed that omission violates the
retained read-after-write contract (F1). The rules below replace it and are the
complete read/write ordering rules.

```javascript
// Composition (read):  flag ─▶ cache.get ─▶ pending-fill token ─▶ single-flight ─▶ repository.read ─▶ guarded fill
// Composition (write): repository.write ─▶ invalidate(key) [always, flag-independent]
const pendingFills = new Map(); // key -> Set<{cancelled:boolean}>; entries exist only while a miss is in flight

async function readProfile(key) {
  if (!cacheFlag.enabledFor(key)) return repository.read(key);           // F10: flag gates reads only
  const cached = cache.get(key);                                          // undefined = miss or adapter bypass
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached === ABSENT ? null : cached;      // F4: unwrap sentinel (null = existing absent result)
  const token = { cancelled: false };
  track(pendingFills, key, token);
  let value;
  try {
    value = await singleFlight.run(key, () => repository.read(key));      // existing wrapper; releases on failure
  } finally {
    untrack(pendingFills, key, token);
  }
  if (token.cancelled) {                                                  // F1: a write invalidated this key mid-read
    metrics.inc('profile_cache_fill_cancelled_total');
  } else {
    cache.set(key, value === null ? ABSENT : value);                      // adapter applies 10 s / 30 s TTL, byte cap, oversize reject (F6)
  }
  return value;                                                           // caller keeps its own snapshot (allowed by contract)
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  let saved;
  try {
    saved = await repository.write(key, update);
  } catch (err) {
    if (isIndeterminateWriteError(err)) invalidate(key, 'write_indeterminate'); // F2: DB state unknown
    throw err;                                                                   // existing typed mapping unchanged
  }
  invalidate(key, 'write_committed');
  return saved;
}

function invalidate(key, reason) {
  for (const t of pendingFills.get(key) ?? []) t.cancelled = true;       // (a) in-flight fills must not land
  singleFlight.detach(key);                                              // (b) later readers start a fresh DB read
  cache.delete(key);                                                     // (c) drop PRESENT or ABSENT entry
  metrics.inc('profile_cache_invalidate_total', { reason });
}
```

`isIndeterminateWriteError` maps the repository's existing typed errors: validation,
authorization, not-found and conflict rejections are deterministic pre-commit
failures and preserve the cache; timeout, connection-lost, and any unrecognised
class are indeterminate and invalidate. Unknown defaults to invalidate.
`singleFlight.detach(key)` is added to the existing wrapper if it lacks one: the
in-flight promise still resolves to its existing waiters (they began before the
commit); the slot is simply no longer joinable.

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, and authorization. New wrapper tests cover hit/miss,
eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure fallback, successful-write
invalidation, failed-write preservation, and concurrent-miss coalescing.

`[Amended: F1, F2, F6, F10]` Additional wrapper tests: the four async schedules
S1–S4 (Section 4) with controlled pause/release points; failed-write behaviour split
into deterministic-rejection preservation and indeterminate-error invalidation;
oversize value rejected without evicting others; flag percentage change yields an
empty cache; write on an unflagged key still invalidates. Assertions are listed in
Section 6.

The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,

and writes bypass the cache while disabled, and enabling creates an empty cache.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors

of flag state (a no-op on an empty cache). Deploy ships with the flag off; the owner
enables 10% only after confirming exactly one process is serving.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.
